messages:
sarah: Quick heads-up — we need to finalize the customer-facing validation and docs for the upcoming audit-event coverage change. This impacts KMS key use events and RBAC grant/revoke. Who can pair on a blurb for the changelog? :page_with_curl:
omar: I can draft the changelog entry and the migration notes. Two questions: 1) Do we guarantee old event IDs for 90 days? 2) Any new required fields for downstream SIEMs?
tess: We agreed to keep old event_types stable but add a `schema_version` field. We'll support v1 and v2 concurrently for 60 days, then v1 becomes deprecated — noted in the rollout plan.
mike: On KMS side, the only structural change is adding `kms_key_alias` and `kms_key_fingerprint` to audit events when keys are used for encrypt/decrypt. Those are non-sensitive metadata (no raw keys). That should be fine for customers that forward to external SIEMs.
sarah: Good. Omar please add both the deprecation window and the fallback behavior (if consumer doesn't send schema_version assume v1). Also include example events.
julie: I'll own the docs page and the changelog anchor. Omar, can you post a short sample payload we can paste into the docs and the API contract checker? We should include a tiny JSON schema snippet so our validator flags missing fields.
omar: Sample below — small and intentionally minimal for customers to copy/paste:
```json
{
  "schema_version": "2",
  "event_type": "kms.key_usage",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-12T17:03:22Z",
  "actor": {
    "id": "user_123",
    "role": "service_account"
  },
  "resource": {
    "type": "kms_key",
    "id": "alias/redwood/prod",
    "alias": "alias/redwood/prod",
    "fingerprint": "sha256:abcd..."
  },
  "action": "encrypt",
  "outcome": "success"
}
```
tess: Perfect. For RBAC changes: audit events for `rbac.grant` and `rbac.revoke` will include `role_changed` and `scope` fields. Make sure customers know we now emit both `target_role_id` and `target_role_name` to help mapping.
mike: Quick vuln-triage note: if any consumer ingests `fingerprint` and treats it as secret, we must add a note in docs telling them not to treat it as a credential. It is non-sensitive by design but could be sensitive in weird regulatory contexts.
sarah: Good catch. Add a line in the changelog and the validation docs: "Do not consider `fingerprint` a secret; it's metadata only."
sec-bot: Planned rollout: 2026-03-25 03:00 UTC. Canary to 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 12 hours. Autorevert on error rate spike > 2x baseline. See: https://go/redwood/rollouts/5678
julie: I'll draft the customer message. Draft subject: "Upcoming change to audit event schema — action recommended if you forward events to SIEMs". Short bullets + copy/paste example.
omar: Also adding a small validation CLI to `tools/audit-validate` so customers can run locally before upgrading. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/audit-schema/pulls/4321 — includes JSON Schema and test harness.
tess: Ops: ensure Splunk and Datadog forwarders accept the new optional fields; add mapping note. I'll run a quick test today.
mike: For KMS integration we need to ensure HSM-backed keys are represented the same way; I'll confirm with infra and add to docs if anything differs.
sarah: Action items: Omar draft changelog + sample payload (ETA EOD), Julie draft customer email (ETA tomorrow AM), Tess validate forwarders and RBAC field mapping (ETA EOD), Mike confirm HSM/KMS parity (ETA EOD). I'll own the rollout and incident playbook updates.
omar: On it. I'll include a short migration checklist for customers and a validator link in the email.
julie: Thx — will sync with PM for the audience list. :thumbsup:
sarah: Great, if nothing else, we'll collate PR links and ship the changelog by tomorrow. Ping here if you hit blocker.
